sketches.mechanism: Optional chaining — accessing a property through a chain of optionals returns nil and silently stops evaluation the moment any link is absent
sketches.resonance: A lineage of belonging that dissolves into nothing the instant one ancestor is missing, like memory that cannot reach past a lost generation.

sketches.mechanism: In Lua, table indices start at 1, and accessing index 0 returns nil — the zeroth position simply does not exist
sketches.resonance: Before the beginning there is nothing; the first moment is already 1, and whatever came before it cannot be found.
sketches.draft:
local life = {}
life[1] = true
life[2] = true
life[3] = true

local before_the_beginning = life[0]
-- nil

sketches.mechanism: The 'never' type represents values that can never occur; a function returning 'never' cannot return at all, and a variable of type 'never' cannot be assigned anything
sketches.resonance: A promise so absolute it can never be fulfilled — the type system itself forbids any possible value from satisfying it.
